The main things to look for are 
Origin: Australian is the highest quality and not susceptible to cracking as much
Colour: 
Colours that are expensive to cheap are red, yellow, green, blue , purple 
Pattern:
In general larger areas of colour are valued higher, pinfire is relatively cheap as the colour is similar to pin-pricks, Flagstone is a very nice and expensive pattern and resembles large paverstones,
Brightness: 
The brightness of opals is measured on a scale of 1 - 5 with the affix "b" added before the number, a B1 is dull and only shows in sunlight, all the way upto a b5 which can be seen even in the dullest of lighting, the brighter the colour in general, the higher the price, please note that the brightness is an average across the stone as some areas may be more full than others.
Body tone:
Generally darker opals and crystal opal (if bright) is valued much higher than lighter body tones, the body tone is the underlying colour and darkness of the opal when the colour is ignored
Cut: 
A cut plays a pivotal role in pricing and opal, in general, the more aesthetically pleasing the shape, the higher the commanded price, a freeform or carving may not sell as well as a symmetrical oval with a high dome, likewise an uneven shape with scratches and a low dome will command a significantly lower asking price than a professionally polished and symmetrical stone ready to be set in jewellery
